privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.temporary: Contact details pending — the privacy contact email will be published on this page soon, and until then there is no approved email address for requests.
privacy.body: This policy explains what data the platform collects, why, who can see it, and what never happens to it. It is written from the practices documented for the platform, and where something has not yet been decided we say so explicitly instead of assuming it.

sections.heading: Who operates the platform and who this policy covers
paragraphs: This platform is operated by Palestine Post (the “Operator”). This policy covers the iOS and Android apps built for the organization's accredited reporters and field crews, and the web interface used by newsroom staff and by organizations that buy licensed material.
Accounts are issued by the Operator; the apps do not offer self-registration. This policy takes effect on: 1 November 2026.

sections.heading: The data we collect
paragraphs: Account and sign-in data: to sign in, the apps send your email, your password and, when two-factor authentication is enabled on the account, a six-digit code from your authenticator. The server keeps the password only as a one-way hash, never in readable form. Apart from that, email is the only contact information the apps rely on, and they do not ask for your legal name. For buyer organizations on the web we record the organization's details (legal name, display name, country, billing email and seat count) and the email and role of its members.

Uploaded material: the video and photo files a reporter chooses manually, together with the fixed fields and the desk form attached to them. The fixed fields are the title, the material types, the governorate and the city (both required, typed as text: an approximate place, not coordinates), the priority, three sensitivity questions (minors, injuries, graphic scenes) and the display name. The reporter chooses the display name for each material: their real name, a pseudonym they type themselves, or the network's name. The apps send that choice, and the pseudonym text only if one is chosen; they do not ask for or send the reporter's legal name. Authorized staff see the display name together with the material.

File and technical data: when an upload starts, the app sends the file's name as it appears on the device, its type and its size, together with a SHA-256 checksum of the whole file that the server compares after assembling it. The Android app also sends checksums of the first and last megabyte, used only to spot duplicates.

Notification identifiers: a randomly generated installation UUID that is not derived from device identifiers, together with an APNs token on iOS or an FCM token on Android, and the platform and app version. They are used only to send notifications. The apps do not collect the advertising identifier or persistent hardware identifiers.

App integrity token: a short-lived verification token (App Attest on iOS, Play Integrity on Android) that shows an upload request comes from a genuine copy of the app and passes through the operating system's services. We do not use it to track you.
On the web: a single session cookie that page scripts cannot read, valid for eight hours, used to keep you signed in.

sections.heading: The original file and precise location
paragraphs: The original file is uploaded exactly as the camera recorded it, without compression or re-encoding, and its metadata is not stripped before upload, so that its digital fingerprint (SHA-256) is preserved and we can verify the material arrived complete. The original may therefore carry the location, time and device model the camera recorded.

The original is stored on the Operator's servers as it arrived, including the camera location if present, and is not modified. It is never shown in raw form and never delivered to any buyer. Stripping happens in the derivatives the server produces (previews, thumbnails and delivered copies): every processing step produces a new file free of location and revealing data, while the original stays preserved with its fingerprint.

Precise location: the apps do not request the location permission from the operating system, do not read your device's location, and do not send coordinates of their own, neither in the material's fields nor anywhere else. Precise location can reach the platform only inside the metadata of the original file you choose, if the file carries it (for example what the camera recorded); this holds for both the Android and iOS apps, since neither strips the original. We treat it as collected for the apps' function and do not use it for tracking. The server interface can also store optional coordinates entered in a material's fields, encrypted at field level, but neither app nor the web interface sends them. The governorate and city you type are an approximate place, not precise location.

Precise coordinates and protected source names are visible only to someone the administration has granted a separate permission for each, with no default grant to any role; every grant, revocation and actual read is recorded in an audit log.

sections.heading: How we use your data
paragraphs: We use it to receive field material and verify its integrity, to review and produce it editorially, to tell the reporter the status of their material, to license it to buyer organizations, to calculate reporters' earnings, and to protect the platform from forged requests.

We do not sell personal data, we do not use it for advertising, we do not track users across other apps or websites, and we do not share it with data brokers or advertising networks. Licensing material to buyer organizations is described in the section “Licensing to buyer organizations”.

sections.heading: Phone notifications
paragraphs: We use push notifications only for work and account alerts, never for advertising. These include: a change in the status of a material for its reporter (for example when a supervisor has seen it), the receipt for the reporter, incoming-material and escalation alerts for editorial staff, an alert to the account owner when recovery of their account is requested or completed, and an alert to administrators when a sensitive setting changes. The server builds the notification text from fixed templates that carry the short material number or a request number, so it carries no material title, names or locations.

The device is registered for notifications when you sign in. The notification token is stored encrypted, never enters any payload and is never returned in any response, and the device is unregistered when you sign out. On Android, denying the notification permission stops only their display, and the device is still registered; on iOS the notification token is requested only if you allow notifications, so denying means no token is registered.
Any external alert channel the Operator turns on, such as email or text messages, carries the material number and status only.

sections.heading: Who sees the material
paragraphs: Material is processed on the Operator's servers and seen by authorized editors and reviewers according to their role permissions, their scope (office or governorate) and source-protection rules; what falls outside a user's scope is not shown to them.

The apps neither ask for nor send a reporter's legal name. If a legal name is recorded on the account, it is stored encrypted and shown only to someone who holds the permission the administration has set for it: by default a separate permission that nobody holds until it is granted, or, if the administration chooses, the protected-source permission. Every read of it is recorded in the audit log, and it never enters notifications, events or exports. Every sensitive operation is recorded in an audit log that cannot be edited: who did it and when.

sections.heading: Artificial intelligence and external providers
paragraphs: Automated processing, such as transcription and shot detection, is used to prepare drafts that a person reviews and decides on.

Material tagged as sensitive is never sent to any external provider; it is processed locally on the Operator's servers or manually, and the platform chooses the route from the sensitivity tag automatically.

Material not tagged as sensitive may pass through an external processing provider for technical processing under the Operator's rules, and the Operator requires any external provider to accept institutional terms that bar it from training on the material. Until the administration approves a written policy on what may be sent externally, automated processing runs locally.

sections.heading: Licensing to buyer organizations
paragraphs: Material may be licensed, according to its rights and by the Operator's decision, to buyer media organizations, and this sharing does take place. The buyer receives copies produced on the server with their metadata stripped, and the raw original is never delivered. The buyer also sees the listing details of the material: its title, description, shot list, material types, governorate, shooting date (without the time of day), duration and dimensions, the licence terms, and a credit line. The governorate is coarse location. Buyers never see precise location: no GPS coordinates, no city, no device identifiers, no protected source names and no reporter identity. The display name the reporter chose, including a pseudonym, is not delivered to buyers: the credit line is a single network name set by the Operator.

Every final copy is checked before delivery (its metadata and any accompanying provenance data) to make sure it reveals no protected identity or location. Download links are signed and short-lived, and previews carry a watermark.
Each sale keeps a record of the licence terms, the price and the version the buyer agreed to, and the public verification page shows only the licence number, its status and its validity.

sections.heading: Payments at this stage
paragraphs: At this stage payments run on a test payment provider in test mode only: no real money moves and no real payout channel is enabled. Choosing the real provider and payout channels is a later decision that has not yet been made.

The payment page is hosted by the provider; card details never pass through our servers and are not stored in any log, and you should not enter a real card in test mode. We keep the order record (items, amount, status, dates and the buying organization) and the licence record, and the test provider learns only the order number and amount.
Reporters' payout requests are also test-only: no real money and no bank details.

sections.heading: Retention, deletion and backups
paragraphs: The original is kept unmodified with its fingerprint. Deleting the local copy from a reporter's phone after the receipt is the reporter's own decision. The app offers an emergency wipe of the session data, queues and local receipts.
Encrypted backups of the platform's data are kept, so deleted data may remain in backups until their retention period ends.
The audit log and the financial ledger entries are append-only and are not edited, and sales records and invoices remain even when a sold item is withdrawn.

Retention periods: materials and their originals are kept with no automatic deletion period while the archive operates, and the original is never modified. Any other deletion is handled on request through the contact email given in the section “Your rights and how to reach us”, and no periods are stated here for any other records.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: We protect your data with controls that include an encrypted connection, field-level encryption of GPS coordinates and notification tokens, the least privilege possible for each role, and signed short-lived links. The Android app blocks screenshots and the app preview in the recent-apps list, and the iOS app offers an optional app lock.

sections.heading: Your rights and how to reach us
paragraphs: You can ask the Operator to let you see, correct or delete your data, or ask about this policy, by the privacy contact email: {email}. We consider each request and tell you what can be deleted and what must be kept for legal, editorial, financial or security reasons, such as sales records, invoices and the audit log.
You can also delete the local copy on your phone at any time, sign out to unregister your device from notifications, and run the emergency wipe.
Operator: Palestine Post. Jurisdiction and hosting location: Palestinian law, with GoDaddy as the hosting provider. The current version of this policy is published on this page.
